task: Implement GitHub issue #19 in the static React ebook viewer: a corner hover preview that is still up (no mousemove after it appeared, e.g. the pointer left the window) is completed as a page turn when the view mode switches (spread <-> single page) in a very small window, because the app's settle() calls stopMove with hovering=false. Fix in the existing controller.stopMove wrapper in Viewer.tsx onInit: treat the fold as a preview when hovering is true OR controller.getState() === 'fold_corner', and drop it (existing dropFold) instead of turning when pos.x <= 0. Add getState to the controller type. Leaving the preview drawn at normal sizes is out of scope.

context.observed_behavior: Reproduced on main 39944ce: 1440x160, hover bottom-right corner, no further mouse event, resize to 60x160 -> #/p/45 becomes #/p/46 (5/5); left corners -> #/p/42. At normal sizes the preview stays drawn but no page turns. Runtime-injected fix kept #/p/45 in every failing trial.
context.contracts: No external API. page-flip 2.0.7 source vendored in web/node_modules (pinned in web/package-lock.json). Static site, no auth, no persisted data.
context.test_setup: vitest pure-function tests only (web/src/book.ts); no jsdom or e2e. Verification is a scripted Chromium (Playwright) check against `vite preview`, as for PR #14 and PR #17. CI runs `cd web && npm test && npm run build` and `cd web && npm run lint`; main 39944ce passed CI.
context.consumers: Viewer.tsx is the app's single UI component, imported only by web/src/main.tsx; nothing is published as a library.
context.testing_facts: The defect has a faithful reproducer only in a real browser: single-step mouse move onto a corner then a viewport resize across the spread/single threshold. No unit seam; no test infrastructure is to be added.

testing_evidence.test_seam: substantial_setup: no unit seam for the Viewer component; scripted browser check
